articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Proposes Demolition of Seven Blocks in Lower Falinge
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing plans to demolish seven blocks of flats in Lower Falinge to construct 270 new homes, as part of a long-term regeneration initiative aimed at improving the area.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has proposed the demolition of seven blocks of flats in the Lower Falinge estate, which will facilitate the construction of 270 new homes. The blocks identified for demolition include Ollerton, Newstead, Romsey, Quinton, Ullesthorpe, Zeburgh, and Vaynor, all of which RBH has determined are no longer fit for purpose after decades of use.

This initiative is part of a broader regeneration effort that has been ongoing for over a decade. Lower Falinge has faced significant challenges, including being named the most deprived area in England for five consecutive years starting in 2013. In 2016, former Prime Minister David Cameron referred to it as a 'sink estate', highlighting the severe social and economic issues faced by its residents. The current proposal aims to provide a net gain of 150 homes, despite previous demolitions in the area that have reduced the overall housing stock.

In addition to the new housing, RBH plans to enhance public spaces and improve connectivity to Rochdale town centre by adding cycle lanes and footpaths. Most of the new homes will be built on the land currently occupied by the flats set for demolition, with additional plots identified for development on adjacent land near St Mary’s Gate. Before submitting an official planning application to Rochdale Council, RBH has prepared an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) to address potential environmental and social impacts of the proposed development.

Currently, the Zeburgh block is the only one still occupied, with Andy Roche and his partner being the last residents. They are part of a campaign group opposing the demolition, although the lack of residents in the other blocks has made it challenging to gather support. Previous attempts to halt demolition plans were successful, but RBH has since developed a comprehensive housing and regeneration plan, which they believe addresses earlier concerns. Hannah Fleming, RBH's director of regeneration and asset improvement, expressed commitment to creating a safe and affordable community in Lower Falinge, with plans to submit the application in early autumn.

articles.title: Full house for National Emergency Briefing screening in Falinge
articles.excerpt: A community screening of the National Emergency Briefing attracted a full room in Falinge, with Rochdale councillors Tricia Ayrton and Shah Wazir joining residents for the event and discussion afterwards.
articles.content_html:
A community screening of the National Emergency Briefing attracted a full room in Falinge, with two Rochdale Council portfolio holders joining residents for the event and subsequent discussion.

Organisers have thanked everyone who attended the screening, saying it was encouraging to see such a strong turnout for the film and the conversation which followed.

Rochdale Borough Council portfolio holders Councillor Tricia Ayrton and Councillor Shah Wazir were among those attending.

Organisers thanked both councillors for remaining after the screening to listen to residents, take part in discussions and consider how the issues raised by the film could be discussed more widely.

They said the councillors left the event with a plan to help ensure the film and its message reach a broader audience.

The National Emergency Briefing brings together scientists, campaigners and public figures to discuss climate change and the risks they believe the UK faces, with contributors associated with the project including environmental campaigner Chris Packham.

The Falinge event gave residents an opportunity not only to watch the presentation together but to discuss its arguments and what they could mean at a local level.

Following the strong turnout, another community screening has already been arranged.

The next screening will take place on Thursday, September 4 at 6pm, giving residents who were unable to attend the latest event another opportunity to see the film and join the discussion.

Organisers thanked residents, guests and councillors for supporting the event and helping create what they described as an important community conversation.
